activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say:  Ñiŋ lookuŋo ǹ na walaadaa kuŋo mu "daafeŋolu" le ti. Kuwolu  mennu be ñiŋ 
walaadaa kono, ì be dendiŋ, ñiŋ ǹ na walaadaa le la. 
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Munne  mu ñiŋ ti? 
• Call on a pupil at random to answer.
• Say: I si muŋ ne fo noo n ye ñiŋ to?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: Ñiŋ feŋolu be looriŋ ye munne  daa to?
• Give pupils one minute to think. You may suggest they close their eyes to picture 
their response. Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on 
3 pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go 
around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or 
have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the 
week.

Alphabet I-Spy
• Gather all of the letter cards of the letters that have been learned. Place the letter 
cards in different places around the room where the pupils can see the pictures.
• Give pupils a minute to look around to see where the picture cards have been 
placed.
• Say: £ be naa feeyaa le kela, ì ka a fo meŋ ye ko,''yoofiroo". N be  naa kuloo too 
fo la, niŋ i ye wo kuloo la nataaloo je, podi i ye nataaloo coodi. Ali ŋà doolu ke. ÿa 
kumoo je le meŋ ye /a/ kulukaŋo soto.
• Give pupils a chance to find the picture.
• Say:  alimooroo/ kumoo ka dati ñiŋ /a/ kuloo le la. Ali ŋà a fo ñoola 'a', 'alimooroo' 
• Repeat two times slowly while pointing to the keyword.
• Continue with a few keywords. Be sure to go over letters that have been learned 
thus far.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Learning Letter:   "a" "A" 
• Write the small letter "a" very big on the board. Point to the letter.
• Say: Ñiŋ ne mu kuloo ti ¥ be ¥ munafaŋ na meŋ na ñiŋ lookuŋo kono. Ñiŋ "a" kuloo 
le ka /a/ kulukaŋo dii ǹ na. Ali ŋà a fo ñoola /a/ 
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 
times slowly.
• Write the capital letter "A" very big on the board. Point to the capital letter.
• Say: Ñiŋ ne mu a te /a/ kulu kiliŋo ti. A ka /a/ kulukaŋo le fo. Ǹ ka a je diyaamoo, 
moo too waraŋ dulaa too datidulaa to le.
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 
times slowly.
• Point to the small letter "a" on the board or letter card again.
• Say: Waati doolu, ǹ ka a je tenne kumoolu kono.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: £ be naa ǹ toolu saferiñaa le karanna. Janniŋ ¥ be a dati la, ¥ be ¥ buloolu 
mammamdi la le.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 
10 seconds. Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters 
correctly. Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for 
the pupil to trace.

lessons.homework:
• Ask learners to teach their family members the letter name and sound they learnt 
today.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: Ali ŋà a miira, taaliŋo be kela munne  ti?
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: Ali hakiloolu kono, ali nataaloo dedaa ali la miira fee taaliŋo be na kela menti. 
Ali halikiloolu ye munne je? 
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
are visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. 
Choose a good example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.
• Say: Saayiŋ, Ali ŋà nataaloolu juubee mennu be taaliŋo kono ì be ñaameŋ.

• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Ali ye mu ne je nataaloo kono, meŋ niŋ ali la miiroo mulunta.
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at 
random asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the 
picture and the story.
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Niŋ ¥ be karanna, ǹ ka kumoolu kiliŋ-kiliŋ karaŋ ne. Taaliŋo ye kuma jamaalu 
le soto, ǹ ka mennu kiliŋ-kiliŋ karaŋ kayiti wo kayiti bala.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud (TRANSLATE)  
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
Taaliŋo niŋ Jii Siijuloo 
Taaliŋ, Taaliŋ, taalindiŋ ñaamendiŋ doo le sotota nuŋ, meŋ too mu Naayisatu ti. Luŋ 
doo tiloo kandita baake, mindoo ye Taaliŋo muta baake. Mindoo ye a muta baake, a 
lafita i minna.
Naayisatu ko, 'n be samaa batu la,' bari luŋo jamaa tambita, hani    wo samaa maŋ 
naa. Tiloo ka tu faatiyariŋ, aniŋ foñoo ka tara feekaŋ, bari samaa manke.
Taaliŋo naata i miira ka taa jiyo ñiniŋ. A taamata kenoolu kono, a seleta konkoolu kaŋ 
santo. A ye jamboolu niŋ yiroolu koto juubee fo a be jiyo je la, bari a maŋ jiyo je,
Wo kono, Naayisatu ye feŋ kaawakuwo je yiroo koto. Wo naata ke siijulu faa jiyo ti 
meŋ be
motosiŋ kotoo kono. A borita a kaŋ, a ko, "n si n minnoo ñaadii le ñiŋ siijuloo kono." 
Taaliŋo ye a kata, ka payipoo taa ka jiyo saba, bari a daa dooyaata baake le. A maŋ 
jiyo soto noo. A ye beroo taa ka motosiŋo buŋ a ye a ñenkelendi, ka jiyo yelema, bari a 
buloolu lamfuta baake. Bari, hanisaayi jii maŋ naa.

miiroo soto, a ye katandiŋolu kiliŋ-kiliŋ joloŋ siijuloo kono. Domandiŋ domandiŋ, jiyo 
ye a dati ka sele santo, santo.
Labaŋo la, jiyo naata futa siijuloo santo. Taaliŋo jimita siijuloo kaŋ, a ye i miŋ, a ye 
i miŋ fo mindoo bota a la. A seewoota le ko, a te le ye koleyaa kuwo bondi. Taaliŋo 
kontaaniriŋo taata. Ka i paree sila doo kamma.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All

• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the 
following factual questions:
• Question 1: Naayisatu ka munne  ñiniŋ? (jaabiroo; jiyo) 
• Question 2: A ye jiyo tara mintoo le? (jaabiroo; siijuloo kono.)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help 
pupils find the part of the story that contains the answer.
Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Taaliŋ wo taaliŋ ye walaakuŋo le soto. Kuwo kuŋo faŋo  mu menti wo le mu 
taaliŋo mu menti. Taaliŋo be meŋ yitandi kaŋ wo le mu Naayisatu be jiyo le ñiniŋ 
kaŋ. Ñiŋ ne ye a tinna ŋa a miira ko, taaliŋo mu Naayisatu ye jiyo soto ñaameŋ.
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say: Kuu kummaa mu menti, wo le mu ko,'' Naayisatu aniŋ siijuloo,''wo le mu, 
Naayisatu ye jiyo soto ñaameŋ, taaliŋo bee mu menti wo le mu ko, a la jii ñiniŋñaa.
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the 
story is mostly about.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. 
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly 
spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Ñiŋ mu kulu jumaa le ti? A ka muŋ kulukaŋ ne fo?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that 
have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Niŋ ŋa kulukaŋo fo, aniŋ kuloolu mennu be ali tolu bulu ì keta siifaa kiliŋ ti, i 
niŋ i kafuñoo ye wo kayitoo naati, ali ye wo kuloolu tembendi walaabaa bala. 
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are 
having difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

Name Card
• Gather all the pupil name cards.

• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For 
example, "[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.content:

• Say:  Taaliŋo too le mu  taaliŋo la kuwoo ti. Munne  mu taaliŋo too ti?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct

their answer.

ask them prompting questions, such as: What do you see in the picture? What is

and relate to the story.

activities.content:

card): Who? What? Where? When? Why?

factual question aloud and have the pupil answer.

• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct

• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils each day to answer questions. If a pupil is 
not able to answer, reread the part of the story that has the answer. See if the 
pupil can respond correctly. If not, explain the correct response. Monitor and keep 
track of pupils having difficulty, and consider how to give them extra support.

them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.

have been learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.

name and as they say it move your finger along the letters. Then have the pupil

and those pupils who have difficulty. If pupils don't recognize their name, try to 
find a way to help them remember it. For example, write it in large print on their 
notebook or a piece of spare paper. Ask them to take it home and trace the letters 
with their finger a few times. If pupils have difficulty clapping the syllables in their 
name, clap with them as you slowly say their name.

• WHO: Jumaalu le mankutoo be taaliŋo kono? (Jaabiiroo: Mariyaama, Faatu, 
Laamini aniŋ bariŋo)
• WHAT:  Mariyaama ye munne  karaŋ nuŋ? (Jaabiiroo: A ye suwolu siifa jamaa le 
karaŋ)
• WHERE: Taaliŋo keta minto le? (Jaabiroo: saatee ŋ to)
• WHEN: Waati jumaa le mu  I ye I bariŋ kumpaboo? (Jaabiroo: Soŋ jaabiroolu la 
mennu maŋ kiliŋ)
• WHY: Munne  ye a tinna ǹ ŋà suwolu soto mennu fatata? (Jaabiroo: Soŋ jaabiroolu 
la mennu maŋ kiliŋ)
• WHAT IF:WHAT IF: Fo niŋ I be saabatiriŋ banku buŋo kono, I si weeri palanteroo 
ke noo le baŋ? (Jaabiroo: Soŋ jaabiroolu la mennu maŋ kiliŋ)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Continue 

through all questions. 
• NOTE: Be sure to ask different pupils each day to answer questions. If a pupil is 
not able to answer, reread the part of the story that has the answer. See if the 
pupil can respond correctly. If not, explain the correct response. Monitor and keep 
track of pupils having difficulty, and consider how to give them extra support.

Personal Learning
• Read the title of the story and show the illustration again. 
• Say: Ali ye munne  karaŋ taaliŋo kono? 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they 
learned from the story. Walk around and listen to what pupils are saying.
• After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. Choose a good example you 
heard from a pupil, and have the pupil share it with the class. 
Drawing it Out
• Say: Saayiŋ, n be  na taaliŋo bee fo la kotenke. Niŋ n be  a fo kaŋ, ¥ be a karanna, 
fii feŋolu ka meŋ ñaameŋ domandiŋ - domandiŋ.
• Before reading each paragraph of the story, choose pupils at random to draw out 
on the chalkboard the growth of the seed as you read. Another option: Assign a 
step in the life cycle of the bean seed to 1-2 rows or tables of pupils, so all pupils 
have a part to draw.

Mariyaama be sabatirŋ satewo konoo. Ala buŋo loota bankoo le la aniŋ ñataŋ 
kankaraŋo. Mariyaama ko, "ŋa n na suwoo kanu le, luŋ kiliŋ, Mariyaama bariŋ na ta 
ke kumpaboo. A bariŋ be sabitiriŋ kapitaloo le to. Mariyaama ye a bariŋ ñininka "ì la 
suwo be ñadi le." A bariŋ ko "N be  sabatiriŋ bunjaŋo le santo niŋ n na dinbayaalu. N 
na suwo loota niŋ ceemento le la, aniŋ weeri palanteroolu. N be  bee dendiŋ koridaa le 
la.
Mariyaama sanawu ma Faatu, be sabatiriŋ baadaalaa. Mariyaama taata a kumpaboo. 
Faatu la buŋo be loriŋ baramalu le kaŋ. Mariyaama ye ñininkaroo ke ko "munne  ne 
ye a tnina i la buŋo jamfata santo baake'? Faatu ko, Ñiŋ baa faata samakono, jiyo ka 
siilee santo le. "Baramalu le ka n na buŋo tankadi sinaŋola".
Mariyaama tata a kafuǹoo Laamini kumpaboo. Laamini la dimbaayaa  mu kantarilu le 
ti mennu niŋ ì la koree ka sawuŋ sawuŋ. Laamini be sabatiriŋ dankoroŋ buŋ le kono ye 
meŋ loo dokoolu niŋ basoolu le la. Laamini ko, "nka taa ñaamoo ǹiniŋ ǹ na bula feŋolu 
ye le. Niŋ ǹ na buŋolu ka sawuŋ sawuŋ ne."
Mariyaama ye ì miira buŋolu bee la, a ko "moolu bee la suwo fatata le. Bari koridaa 
wo koridaa ka moolu tankandi a niŋ ke ì hakiloolu tenkundi.
